artifact: CP1 - both mechanisms established, BEFORE a fix is chosen
status: MECHANISMS ESTABLISHED. No product or gate file edited at this checkpoint. The fix design below is a proposal.
whyThisCheckpointExistsBeforeAnyEdit: The dispatch orders the mechanism established before a fix is chosen, because a fix chosen first is a tuning exercise. Both mechanisms below are measured with single-variable arms and both are traced to the axe-core source that produces them. Everything here was measured against main at 3452b31 with NO change to the gate.

mechanism1_viewport.claim: The gate's number is not merely REPORTED against the viewport. axe does not EVALUATE anything outside it, and an element it does not evaluate appears in no bucket at all - not violations, not passes, not incomplete. Silence, read as success.

supersetTest.question: does scanning taller find genuinely DIFFERENT violations, or the same ones later? The dispatch asks this explicitly and it decides the fix.
raw: 1200: +1 -0  gained=["color-contrast tr:nth-child(17) > td:nth-child(3) > .p-ok.pill"] lost=[]
1600: +4 -0  gained=["color-contrast tr:nth-child(18) > td:nth-child(3) > .p-ok.pill","tr:nth-child(19)...","tr:nth-child(20)...","tr:nth-child(21)..."] lost=[]
supersetTest.answer: THE SAME ONES LATER. Every height's flagged set is a strict superset of the height below it and NOTHING is ever lost. The gained targets are successive rows of one table - tr:nth-child(17), then 18, 19, 20, 21 - the same defect appearing row by row as the fold moves down. Growing the viewport reveals; it does not change what a revealed element measures.
supersetTest.whyThatMatters: it licenses growing the viewport as an instrument technique rather than as a different test, and it hands the technique its own divergence test: the reference set MUST be a subset of the full-extent set, and a run where it is not has changed the product rather than revealed it.

theHeightLadder.saturation: at 2400 the last scrollable extent reaches zero and every further height returns an identical figure. The saturation height is a property of the SURFACE, not a constant - see the residual finding below.

whyAxeDoesThis_readAtSource.matcher: colorContrastMatches, axe.js:28619. Its final statement is the gate: `var clippingAncestors = get_overflow_hidden_ancestors_default(virtualNode); return rects.some(function(rect) { var overlaps = visually_overlaps_default(rect, node); if (!clippingAncestors.length) { return overlaps; } var withinOverflow = clippingAncestors.some(function(overflowNode) { return _rectsOverlap(rect, overflowNode.boundingClientRect); }); return overlaps && withinOverflow; });`
whyAxeDoesThis_readAtSource.consequence: an element whose text rects do not overlap the box of an overflow-hidden ancestor is not a CANDIDATE. It never reaches the check, so it cannot be a violation, a pass, or an incomplete. axe's own `outsideViewport` incomplete reason exists at axe.js:24716 and is unreachable on this product for exactly this reason.

raw: h=900  lastPill top=1617 bottom=1637; overflowHiddenAncestors = div.panel(1477..1772), main.shell-main(52..900), #app-shell(0..900), body(0..900)
h=2400 lastPill top=1617 bottom=1637; overflowHiddenAncestors = div.panel(1477..1772), main.shell-main(52..2400), #app-shell(0..2400), body(0..2400)
measuredOnThisProduct.reading: the pill sits at the SAME document position in both arms - top 1617 either way. Nothing moved. What changed is that main.shell-main / #app-shell / body are height:100% with overflow:hidden, so their boxes end at the viewport bottom; at 900 the pill's rect does not overlap them and the matcher drops it, at 2400 it does and the matcher keeps it. The bound is the overflow-hidden clipping box, which on this product IS the viewport because the shell is height:100%.

whyAxeDoesThis_readAtSource.isAFullPageScanPossibleWithThisAxeBuild: NO, not as a mode. axe-core 4.13 has no option that evaluates outside the clipping box, and window scrolling does nothing here because the shell does not scroll - the scrolling happens inside div.colstack. The only lever that puts an element into the evaluated population is making the clipping box taller, which is what growing the viewport does.

theResidualNobodyHasNamed.reading: work-connections carries content past 3000 inside an overflow:HIDDEN container rather than a scrollable one, so a scroll-extent probe reports zero hidden pixels while 96 elements are still clipped away. A height derived from scroll extents would have certified that surface as fully covered. The height must be derived from the ACTUAL out-of-viewport element count, and the stop condition must be the coverage assertion itself.

mechanism2_environment.claim: The Windows/Linux disagreement is FONT METRICS, and specifically whether the remote webfont resolved. It is not device scale factor, not the Chromium build, and not axe. One wrapped line in a sticky nav footer decides whether 88 unresolved nodes exist or zero do.

theSingleVariableArm.countingRule: unresolved NODES = axe incomplete entries on conformance-tagged rules, summed over all 46 scans; one element unresolved on ten scans counts ten. 88 = 2 nodes (#nav-demonstrated and #nav-sources-rule) on each of 44 scans.
theSingleVariableArm.reconciliationWithR2: R2 reported 44 unresolved nodes locally on Windows. 88 / 2 themes = 44 per theme, which is R2's figure exactly. Two independent measurements of the same thing, agreeing once the counting rule is stated. R2's number was never wrong; it was a per-theme figure read as a total.
theSingleVariableArm.andTheUNMODIFIEDGateAgrees: the gate itself, unmodified, on main at 3452b31, run locally on Windows tonight: `a11y gate FAILED: color-contrast [light]: 44 unresolved node(s) exceeds the 1 adjudicated as elmPartiallyObscuring ...; color-contrast [dark]: 44 unresolved node(s) exceeds the 1 adjudicated ...`, real exit code 1. Raw at P:/tmp/k2-work/baseline-main-local.log. The sweep PREDICTED 88 before the gate was run, which is a pre-registered band met rather than a number arrived at.

webfont BLOCKED probeW=208.80

raw: allowed: nav {navClientH:848, navScrollH:966, navHiddenPx:118, footTop:601, footH:299, provLines:274, demRect{top:640,h:36}}
blocked: nav {navClientH:848, navScrollH:928, navHiddenPx: 80, footTop:619, footH:281, provLines:256, demRect{top:658,h:36}}
theGeometryThisProduces.reading: the wider glyphs wrap the nav footer's .prov to exactly ONE more 18px line (256 -> 274), which makes the sticky .nav-foot 18px taller (281 -> 299), which moves its figures 18px up (658 -> 640) and increases how much of the scrolling nav list it covers (80 -> 118 hidden px). web/shell.css gives .nav-foot position:sticky with an OPAQUE background over that list, which is the overlap G-95 already identified - this names what MOVES it.

whyAxeTurnsThatIntoAnUnresolvedCheck_rea.sampler: getRectStack2, axe.js:24678, samples the element stack at the centre of EACH text line box via get_text_element_stack_default, not at a single point. filteredRectStack, axe.js:24693, compares those stacks: `if (!isSame) { incomplete_data_default.set('bgColor', 'elmPartiallyObscuring'); return null; }` at axe.js:24710-24713.
whyAxeTurnsThatIntoAnUnresolvedCheck_rea.consequence: an element whose wrapped lines sit over DIFFERENT things has no single resolvable background and axe correctly refuses to guess. Full coverage and no coverage both resolve; only PARTIAL coverage fires. It is a knife-edge predicate on a layout detail.

raw: /?cityKey=empty-city  webfont=BLOCKED  probeW=208.8  demRect={top:694,bottom:730}  distinctCornerStacks=1   (all four -> #nav-demonstrated > a.prov > div.nav-foot > #shell-nav > div.shell-body)

/?cityKey=empty-city  webfont=ALLOWED  probeW=228.33 demRect={top:694,bottom:730}  distinctCornerStacks=2   (top corners -> ... > a.navitem > div.navgroup; bottom corners -> ... > #shell-nav > div.shell-body)
measuredAtThePredicate.reading: the element's own box is IDENTICAL in both arms - top 694, bottom 730. Only what is behind it moved, because the nav list's scroll extent changed with the font. A nav item's bottom edge slid across the figure's top edge and the stacks stopped agreeing.
measuredAtThePredicate.honestLimit: the corner probe is a four-point approximation of axe's per-line-box sampler, so it corroborates rather than reproduces: on /?lens=finance the corner probe reads one stack in both arms while axe reports 2 nodes in the allowed arm. The primary evidence is the axe-level arm - 0 versus 88 over 46 scans with one variable changed - not the corner probe.

reconciliationWithTheTwoPriorMeasurement.G95onLinuxCI: 2 nodes total, on empty-city-overview ALONE, both themes. Its REVIEW_ITEMS pin is {light: 1, dark: 1}.
reconciliationWithTheTwoPriorMeasurement.K2onWindowsWithTheWebfont: 88 nodes = 44 per theme, on 22 of 23 surfaces - and ZERO on empty-city-overview, which is the ONE surface G-95's Linux run fires on.
reconciliationWithTheTwoPriorMeasurement.theInversionIsTheEvidence: empty-city carries the longest footer sentence in the product, so its .prov is already the tallest; adding a wrapped line moves its figures past the last nav item into FULL coverage, which resolves. On every other surface the same line moves the figures INTO partial coverage, which does not. A predicate that flips in opposite directions on different surfaces for the same one-line change is not a number anyone can pin, and that is the control-design finding rather than a tuning target.
reconciliationWithTheTwoPriorMeasurement.whatIsStillOpenAndHowItCloses: what Linux CI actually renders - whether it resolves the webfont at all and what its advance widths are - cannot be measured from this machine. It closes by shipping the witness (probeW, nav geometry, platform, chromium build) in the scanner's own per-run output and READING IT OFF THE CI LOG on this lane's own PR. That is the move G-95 made with its colour witness, which turned 'two machines disagree' into a one-line diagnosis.

theFixIPropose.shapeFirst: The gate stops asserting a number and starts stating the conditions under which the number is true. Both mechanisms above are conditions, and neither is currently written anywhere a reader of the figure sees it.
theFixIPropose.1_viewportBecomesADeclaredDimension: A scan is a surface x a THEME x a VIEWPORT, and the viewport list is exported and declared: `reference` 1440x900 (the height the baseline was taken at and the fold a person reads) and `full-extent` 1440xH where H is DERIVED per surface by growing until the out-of-viewport element count reaches zero, capped and reported. Both run in one page load - grow, re-run axe, restore - so the added cost is one axe run rather than a second navigation and a second keyboard walk.
theFixIPropose.2_theCoverageRatioTravelsWithTheNumber: every scan records evaluated/rendered text elements and the run prints it beside the node count. A figure whose bound is not stated beside it is the DEV_PROCESS 1.2 defect; this makes the bound impossible to quote without.
theFixIPropose.3_theTechniqueGetsItsOwnDivergenceTest: the reference flagged set must be a SUBSET of the full-extent flagged set. Proven above over nine heights, lost=0 at every step. If an element ever fails at reference and passes at full-extent, growing the viewport changed the product rather than revealing it, and the run FAILS.
theFixIPropose.4_pinsBecomePerArm: waivers and adjudications pin per theme x viewport rather than per theme, for the same reason the pin became per theme in G-95: one number lets a full-extent regression hide behind a reference improvement.
theFixIPropose.5_theWebfontMustLandOrTheScanIsUnmeasure: the third landing assertion, beside 'the theme landed' and 'the page painted'. A scan where the shipped typeface did not resolve measured a product nobody ships, and it is recorded as FAILED rather than clean. This is the environment PIN: every authoritative scan is a scan of the shipped face.
theFixIPropose.6_environmentVarianceBecomesPartOfTheCon: an environment block on every run - platform, arch, chromium build, dpr, axe version, the advance-width witness, the nav geometry witness - printed where the numbers are read; an explicit AUTHORITATIVE declaration that the Linux CI job is the figure of record and a local run is indicative; and a local run that SAYS SO in its own output rather than letting a developer read 44 as a real number.
theFixIPropose.7_theKnifeEdgeClassIsAdjudicatedBySubjec: a ceiling on a count that ranges 0 to 88 across two operating systems is a ceiling nobody can set correctly - R2-F7's words, and this lane's measurement agrees. So an environment-dependent adjudication names its SUBJECT and its basis; any unresolved node outside that subject set FAILS, any count inside it is accepted and REPORTED LOUDLY with the environment beside it. It fires on a new subject, which is the real regression, and not on the same subject at a different count, which is the machine.
theFixIPropose.8_aWaiverThisLaneWillNeed: making the gate see the full extent makes it see 5 real AA color-contrast nodes on lens-development-services-inspections [light] that this lane cannot fix: the --sc-ok / --sc-ok-wash pair lives in web/sc-kit.css, which is byte-identical across three repos, is named untouchable by this dispatch, and whose own header says a repo that edits a token value has forked the system. It gets a waiver with a per-arm ceiling, the product-line token pass as owner, the measured ratio as basis, and 'when the kit raises --sc-ok' as the removal condition - and the existing zero arm still fires the moment that lands.

adversarialReviewOfMyOwnDesign: RISK: growing the viewport could change the product rather than reveal it. Answered by measurement (strict superset over nine heights, nothing ever lost) AND by making that a permanent assertion rather than a one-time observation.

RISK: a fixed tall height would ship a second undeclared bound. Answered by the work-connections residual - 96 elements still clipped at 3000 with zero reported scroll extent - which is why the height is derived from the out-of-viewport count and not from scroll extents.

RISK: asserting the webfont landed makes a third-party CDN able to turn CI red. Accepted deliberately: a scan of a page whose typeface did not resolve is an UNMEASURED scan, and this repo has already ruled twice that unmeasured must not read as clean. The failure is loud, self-describing and retried once.

RISK: a subject-bounded adjudication is weaker than a count ceiling and could hide a real regression on the same elements. Accepted with its cost stated: the count is still printed on every run, and the alternative - a ceiling on a figure two machines put at 0 and 88 - makes the gate unrunnable on one of them, which is a dead gate under DEV_PROCESS 2.0.

RISK: the added axe run pushes the CI job past its 20-minute timeout. To be measured before the PR is opened; the axe-only sweep of 46 scans took 92 seconds on this machine, so the added cost is of that order rather than of the keyboard walk's.
